when the plan draws an object in a room.rule: When the plan draws an object in a room that is not built in the model, the furniture stage must identify the object's type and place it in the next agent round.

when a decor item's host piece is not bu.rule: When a decor item's host piece is not built, the decor must be deferred to the next agent round, after the host is re-placed.

when a piece's type is not allowed in it.rule: When a piece's type is not allowed in its room (e.g. a sofa in a bedroom), the reading stage must flag it for re-typing or removal, rather than keeping it unverified.

when a room outline holds the labels of.rule: When a room outline holds the labels of two rooms, the reading must split the outline at the wall between the two labelled zones (or flag the missing wall) instead of keeping one label and dropping the other; a dining zone labelled inside a living room is a separate room or a sub-zone, not a lost label.

when an elevation's openings cannot be c.rule: When an elevation's openings cannot be checked against the plans because the north arrow is missing, the reading must infer the orientation from the plan's north arrow or the site context, and flag the elevation as 'orientation unverified' rather than skipping the check entirely.

a drawn section whose ends do not align.rule: A drawn section whose ends do not align with the roof outline (offset > 0.30 m) or whose roof line is non-monotonic must be flagged as a non-corresponding section and excluded from point-by-point roof checks, rather than failing the check silently.
a drawn section whose ends do not align.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

elevations without a view bearing or sid.rule: Elevations without a view bearing or side must be assigned a default orientation based on their position relative to the plan, or flagged as uncheckable with a clear reason, rather than silently failing the comparison.

when a nightstand cannot be snapped to a.rule: When a nightstand cannot be snapped to a wall due to doors/windows blocking all free places within 1.2 m, the fitting stage should allow a small offset (up to 0.10 m) from the wall or place it freestanding next to the bed, rather than refusing all moves.

the agent must only use material look id.rule: The agent must only use material look IDs that exist in the project's vocabulary; the vocabulary should be exposed to the agent in its context so it does not guess look names.

kitchen fittings (sink, wall cabinets) s.rule: Kitchen fittings (sink, wall cabinets) should be built at the library level (with proper textures and details) rather than falling back to parametric meshes when no library model is available.

toilet models in the library should incl.rule: Toilet models in the library should include seat covers and basic decor (e.g., spare toilet paper) to avoid a sterile, incomplete appearance in renders.

bathroom fixtures and tiles should be se.rule: Bathroom fixtures and tiles should be selected from a higher-quality library set to avoid a cheap, institutional look in renders.

bed models in the library should include.rule: Bed models in the library should include more substantial headboards and frames to avoid a plain, low-profile appearance in client-ready renders.

nightstand models in the library should.rule: Nightstand models in the library should be more stylish and cohesive with the room's furniture set to avoid a generic, unstyled appearance.

door models in the library should includ.rule: Door models in the library should include more detailed handles and finishes to avoid a cheap, generic appearance in stylish projects.

a stair or landing that is the only vert.rule: A stair or landing that is the only vertical circulation of a level must be built with a full parametric stair model (treads, risers, stringers and a proper balustrade), never as a bare platform with a glass guard; a platform-only representation is a defect, not a style choice.

interior doors must be built with a styl.rule: Interior doors must be built with a styled door model (panelled or flush with a proper frame and handle) matching the project's finish, never as a plain flat slab; a generic slab door is a defect in a client presentation.

a floor lamp must be built with a proper.rule: A floor lamp must be built with a proper library model (a real lamp with a shade and stem), never as a low-poly box placeholder; a placeholder lamp is a defect.

exterior wall surfaces and plinths must.rule: Exterior wall surfaces and plinths must be built with textured materials (stone, render, brick) matching the project's finish, never as untextured flat surfaces; bare material is a defect in a client presentation.

a stone path or paving leading to an ent.rule: A stone path or paving leading to an entrance must be built with a textured paving model, never as a rough untextured mesh with visible cracks; a placeholder path is a defect.

untyped drawn pieces must be typed by th.rule: Untyped drawn pieces must be typed by the reading stage before the build stage; the build stage must not silently drop untyped pieces without a record.

a labelled outdoor area (veranda, balcon.rule: A labelled outdoor area (veranda, balcony, terrace) in the documents must be built as a site platform with its drawn outline, even when the outline is open or partially defined; 'no outline' is not a valid reason to drop a labelled site area.

a labelled veranda, balcony or terrace i.rule: A labelled veranda, balcony or terrace in the documents must be built as a site area (floor slab, railing, and a door from the adjacent room) even when its outline is incomplete; an unbuildable outline is a reason to flag the drawing, not to silently drop the element.

a room typed 'other' that the documents.rule: A room typed 'other' that the documents name as a dressing room (soyunma odası) must be furnished as a dressing room (mirror, bench or stool, wardrobe); the 'other' type must not suppress the completeness check for that room.

a room typed 'living' must be furnished.rule: A room typed 'living' must be furnished as a living room (seating plus a table and a focal point such as a TV or media unit); a sofa alone does not satisfy the type.

furniture must match the level it is pla.rule: Furniture must match the level it is placed on: a shoe cabinet belongs at the ground-floor entrance, not in an upper-floor hall, which should instead carry a console, coat hook or bench.

when two openings on the same wall are s.rule: When two openings on the same wall are separated by less than 1.20 m, the layout engine must verify that the intervening wall span can accommodate a 0.60 m clear walkway; if not, it must propose moving one of the openings or adjusting the room layout to create the required clearance.

when a bed's headboard is not flush agai.rule: When a bed's headboard is not flush against a wall (offset > 0.02 m), the layout engine must snap it to the nearest wall if the move is within 0.30 m, or flag it for manual review if the move exceeds the drawn-lock tolerance.

when a piece blocks a door swing, the la.rule: When a piece blocks a door swing, the layout engine must move the piece to the nearest free position that does not intersect the door's swing arc, prioritizing positions along the wall opposite the door.

when a piece blocks a window, the layout.rule: When a piece blocks a window, the layout engine must move the piece to the nearest free position that does not obstruct the window's view or access, prioritizing positions along the wall opposite the window.

when a door and a window on the same wal.rule: When a door and a window on the same wall are separated by less than 1.20 m, the layout engine must verify that the intervening wall span can accommodate a 0.60 m clear walkway; if not, it must propose moving one of the openings or adjusting the room layout to create the required clearance.

when a desk is rendered as a floating sl.rule: When a desk is rendered as a floating slab, the render engine must verify that the model includes legs or support structure; if not, it must swap to a model that includes them.

when a room's main functional pieces are.rule: When a room's main functional pieces are not visible in the render, the camera must be adjusted to include them in the frame, prioritizing a wide-angle lens and a position that captures the entire worktop and appliances.

when a living room lacks a sofa or coffe.rule: When a living room lacks a sofa or coffee table, the layout engine must add a living group (sofa, coffee table, armchairs) to anchor the space, prioritizing a sofa along the longest wall.

when a bathroom's main pieces (toilet, w.rule: When a bathroom's main pieces (toilet, washbasin, bathtub) are not visible in the render, the camera must be adjusted to include them in the frame, prioritizing a wide-angle lens and a position that captures the entire room.

when a kitchen's main functional pieces.rule: When a kitchen's main functional pieces (stove, fridge, wall cabinets) are not visible in the render, the camera must be adjusted to include them in the frame, prioritizing a wide-angle lens and a position that captures the entire worktop and appliances.

when a bathroom's main pieces (shower, t.rule: When a bathroom's main pieces (shower, toilet, washbasin) are not visible in the render, the camera must be adjusted to include them in the frame, prioritizing a wide-angle lens and a position that captures the entire room.

when a bedroom's main pieces (bed, armch.rule: When a bedroom's main pieces (bed, armchair, desk) are not visible in the render, the camera must be adjusted to include them in the frame, prioritizing a wide-angle lens and a position that captures the entire room.

a dressing room (soyunma odasi) of 4-8 m.rule: A dressing room (soyunma odasi) of 4-8 m2 is a valid room type for the dressing group; the placement solver must not reject it as 'no place passes the checks' when the room contains a wardrobe and has at least 0.9 m of clear floor space.

every open staircase (no solid wall on o.rule: Every open staircase (no solid wall on one or both sides) must be built with handrails and balustrades on all open sides to meet safety standards.

for rooms with no windows or very small.rule: For rooms with no windows or very small windows (e.g., dressing rooms, closets), the lighting system must be able to increase light by up to x10, or the camera exposure cap must be raised to +6.00 EV to allow proper exposure.

the architect's rule c1 must include a c.rule: The architect's rule C1 must include a check for walkway widths (G11) to ensure that main walkways from entrance doors are at least 0.80 m wide, and flag any walkway that is below this threshold.

the architect's rule f2 / f3 must includ.rule: The architect's rule F2 / F3 must include a check for furniture blocking doors (F7) to ensure that no furniture blocks a door's swing or walkway, and flag any furniture that does.

the architect's rule e1 must include a c.rule: The architect's rule E1 must include a check for doors that are too high to reach (X3) to ensure that all doors are at a reachable height (e.g., 0.90-2.10 m above the floor), and flag any door that is above this range.

a sofa placed under a sloped ceiling mus.rule: A sofa placed under a sloped ceiling must be fitted to the ceiling clearance at its position (max height = ceiling - 0.05 m); the fit check must reject any model whose height exceeds that clearance before the swap is accepted, and the catalogue must offer at least one sofa variant per room whose height fits the minimum ceiling clearance of the room's sloped zone.

site trees must use high-poly, photoreal.rule: Site trees must use high-poly, photorealistic models from the library (not low-poly lollipop placeholders); the site stage must select tree models that match the project's render quality standard, and the catalogue must include at least one photorealistic tree variant per tree type used in the project.

a piece's free zone in front of it must.rule: A piece's free zone in front of it must not be blocked by another piece; the furniture agent must re-place the blocking piece or the piece itself to restore the clearance.

the main walkway from the entrance door.rule: The main walkway from the entrance door must be at least 0.80 m wide; the furniture agent must re-place pieces to widen the path.

a dresser's back must be on a wall; the.rule: A dresser's back must be on a wall; the furniture agent must re-place it to snap to the wall.

a nightstand must not overlap a bed; the.rule: A nightstand must not overlap a bed; the furniture agent must re-place it to clear the collision.

a bed must have at least 0.60 m of clear.rule: A bed must have at least 0.60 m of clearance on its sides; the furniture agent must re-place it to restore the clearance.

a wardrobe's front use zone must be reac.rule: A wardrobe's front use zone must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway; the furniture agent must re-place it to restore access.

a shower must not stand in front of a wi.rule: A shower must not stand in front of a window; the furniture agent must re-place it to clear the opening.

a sofa's free zone in front of it must n.rule: A sofa's free zone in front of it must not be blocked by another piece; the furniture agent must re-place the blocking piece or the sofa itself to restore the clearance.

a floor lamp must not stand in front of.rule: A floor lamp must not stand in front of a window; the furniture agent must re-place it to clear the opening.

a bathtub's back must be on a wall; the.rule: A bathtub's back must be on a wall; the furniture agent must re-place it to snap to the wall.

a washbasin's back must be on a wall; th.rule: A washbasin's back must be on a wall; the furniture agent must re-place it to snap to the wall.

a washing machine's front use zone must.rule: A washing machine's front use zone must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway; the furniture agent must re-place it to restore access.

the exterior environment must be believa.rule: The exterior environment must be believable for a client presentation; the site must include textured ground, a realistic sky, and high-poly trees.

an opening must have a proper frame; the.rule: An opening must have a proper frame; the correct_geometry tool can fix the opening frame.

a labelled outdoor space (veranda, balco.rule: A labelled outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) that the documents outline or label must be built as a site platform with its own floor and guard, even when it has no enclosing walls; a 'no outline' reason is a loss, not a valid skip.

a bathroom's wet fixtures (basin, toilet.rule: A bathroom's wet fixtures (basin, toilet, tub/shower) must be placed so that no two overlap and each keeps its approach clearance; when the solver reports no free place, the room's layout must be re-solved before the run is accepted.

no furniture may stand in the clear line.rule: No furniture may stand in the clear line of sight through a window or door opening; a piece that blocks an opening's ray must be moved out of the opening's path.

a balcony or veranda slab drawn outside.rule: A balcony or veranda slab drawn outside the outer walls must be built with its support structure (columns or cantilever) and a door from the interior; a slab with a railing but no support and no access door is an incomplete build and must not be left floating.

a downpipe must be modelled with a gutte.rule: A downpipe must be modelled with a gutter connection at its top and a splash block or drain at its base; a bare cylinder is a placeholder and is not an acceptable rain-water detail.

the main entrance must be legible: a cle.rule: The main entrance must be legible: a clear door leaf with handle, a canopy or header, and a defined step or landing; when steps already exist, the fix is to add the missing door-leaf/handle/canopy detail, not to re-set the entrance solution.

every interior camera of a room must fra.rule: Every interior camera of a room must frame the room's document openings (windows and doors); a camera that misses a required opening must be re-aimed to include it.

a washbasin must be at a usable working.rule: A washbasin must be at a usable working height (rim ~0.85 m) and reachable; a generated placeholder model that is wedged behind another fixture must be replaced by a real product and re-placed in the room.

a bathroom door must not open directly i.rule: A bathroom door must not open directly into the fixture cluster; the door swing and the fixtures' approach clearances must be resolved so the door does not block access to the basin or toilet.

a stair opening and landing edge must ha.rule: A stair opening and landing edge must have a complete guard (solid balustrade or glass with a proper handrail and no open gap below); a thin placeholder glass panel with a large open gap is a fall risk and is not an acceptable guard.

the entrance approach (steps, handrails,.rule: The entrance approach (steps, handrails, terrace/landing slab) must be finished with proper materials and textures; raw, untextured concrete geometry and floating slabs are placeholders and are not an acceptable entrance finish.

a door must be modelled as a door (leaf,.rule: A door must be modelled as a door (leaf, frame, handle) and must not be rendered as a different object type (e.g. wall art); when a door is seen as another object in a camera view, the door model is wrong and must be corrected.

a drawn piece must be built at its drawn.rule: A drawn piece must be built at its drawn size and position within tolerance (0.05 m); when the built size differs from the drawing, the piece must be resized to the drawn dimensions.

fix_fixture must accept the string 'draw.rule: fix_fixture must accept the string 'drawn' for center to snap a piece back to its documented footprint, or the inspector must emit the numeric drawn center so the tool can be called.

set_camera must accept kind 'room' as an.rule: set_camera must accept kind 'room' as an alias for 'interior' with a room_id, or the agent must be given the room's bounding box to compute a valid position/target.

the furniture agent must add standard ba.rule: The furniture agent must add standard bathroom accessories (mirror, towel, soap, hardware) to every bathroom as part of its completion set, not just the fixtures.

the furniture agent must add a dressing.rule: The furniture agent must add a dressing room set (bench, mirror, lighting) to every dressing room, not just a wardrobe.

labelled site areas (veranda, balcony, t.rule: Labelled site areas (veranda, balcony, terrace) must be built with an outline, floor, and railing if the documents show them, not left as site records.

small drawn pieces (0.21 x 0.20 m) that.rule: Small drawn pieces (0.21 x 0.20 m) that the AI identifies as potted_plant should be typed as potted_plant, not left untyped.

clusters of drawn pieces larger than 4.5.rule: Clusters of drawn pieces larger than 4.5 m on a side should be marked as not furniture (a group) and not built as a single piece.

if the documents name a dresser in a roo.rule: If the documents name a dresser in a room, the piece should be typed as a dresser, even if the room is a living room.

if the documents name a dresser at a spe.rule: If the documents name a dresser at a specific location, the furniture agent must place it there, even if the nearest free place is more than 1 m away.

a dressing room should be typed as 'dres.rule: A dressing room should be typed as 'dressing_room', not 'other', and furnished as a set (wardrobe + mirror + seating).

when two pieces in the same room overlap.rule: When two pieces in the same room overlap and one is a drawn piece locked in a doorway, the movable piece must be re-placed to a free spot in the room, not the locked one.

the big loop must run at least 2 fix cyc.rule: The big loop must run at least 2 fix cycles when the initial score is below 30 and no cycle has been attempted.

a sofa drawn in a bedroom is a reading e.rule: A sofa drawn in a bedroom is a reading error; the piece should be retyped to a type allowed in a bedroom (e.g., armchair or chaise) or removed if it does not fit the room's program.

a dressing room (soyunma odasi) of 5.9 m.rule: A dressing room (soyunma odasi) of 5.9 m² must have a dressing group (wardrobe, bench, mirror) placed; if no place passes the checks, the room type should be reconsidered or the room enlarged.

a small drawn piece around a level mark.rule: A small drawn piece around a level mark text is a level-mark symbol, not furniture; it should be marked as not furniture.

cameras marked for review must be re-set.rule: Cameras marked for review must be re-set with the correct kind (interior or exterior) and valid position/target.

the set_camera tool must accept 'room' a.rule: The set_camera tool must accept 'room' as a valid kind for interior cameras; the schema should be updated to include 'room' as an option for kind.

a drawn piece that is 0.06 m off the wal.rule: A drawn piece that is 0.06 m off the wall should be allowed to snap to the wall if the move is within 0.1 m; the drawn_lock rule should permit small adjustments for drawn pieces.

a wardrobe that blocks a window should b.rule: A wardrobe that blocks a window should be moved to a free wall span; the clearance_ok rule should not refuse a move if the new position is clear of the window.

a wardrobe whose front use zone is not r.rule: A wardrobe whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway should be moved to a free wall span; the clearance_ok rule should not refuse a move if the new position is clear.

an untyped drawn piece of 1.20 x 0.55 m.rule: An untyped drawn piece of 1.20 x 0.55 m in a living room should be retyped to a type that fits its size and room (e.g., sideboard or console); the retype_piece tool should allow this.

a nightstand that reaches 0.06 m² throug.rule: A nightstand that reaches 0.06 m² through the room outline should be allowed to be moved to a free spot in the room; the inside_room rule should not refuse a move if the new position is inside the room.

a coffee table that clashes with the roo.rule: A coffee table that clashes with the room's wood tones should be swapped to a model that fits the room's palette; the swap_model tool should allow a model that passes the fit rules.

a rule that approves overlapping fixed c.rule: A rule that approves overlapping fixed counters must treat any overlap beyond the 0.03 m cut tolerance as a defect, not a pass.

a clearance rule for wet rooms must chec.rule: A clearance rule for wet rooms must check the free zone in front of bathtubs, washbasins and toilets against the minimum approach width, not only the sides.

a seating rule must verify the free zone.rule: A seating rule must verify the free zone in front of each chair or sofa is unobstructed, not only that the piece fits its room.

a window rule must flag any tall piece (.rule: A window rule must flag any tall piece (above the sill height) placed in front of a window, not only pieces that fully cover the glazing.

the exterior landscape must use a realis.rule: The exterior landscape must use a realistic terrain and tree model (not low-poly placeholder blobs) so that views through doors and windows read as a real site, not a placeholder.

the site stage must reject low-poly plac.rule: The site stage must reject low-poly placeholder vegetation (lollipop/blob trees) and only place library models that match the project's photorealistic render standard; a placeholder asset must never be built into the scene.

the furniture agent must select coffee t.rule: The furniture agent must select coffee table models that match the room's color palette (pale/muted tones) and avoid clashing wood tones like bright honey-oak when the floor is pale.

the site stage must reject low-poly plac.rule: The site stage must reject low-poly placeholder vegetation and only place library models that match the project's photorealistic render standard.

furniture models assigned to pieces in f.rule: Furniture models assigned to pieces in finished rooms must meet a minimum visual fidelity standard appropriate to the project's style; placeholder or low-detail models are prohibited.

bed groups in bedrooms should be symmetr.rule: Bed groups in bedrooms should be symmetric (nightstand on both sides) unless spatial constraints explicitly prevent it; the layout solver must verify this symmetry during placement.

paired furniture items (like armchairs).rule: Paired furniture items (like armchairs) must use the same model or a visually coherent set to ensure stylistic consistency.

floor lamps must be selected with a scal.rule: Floor lamps must be selected with a scale appropriate to the room's ceiling height and must not obstruct window views or door swings; models with oversized shades or incorrect proportions are prohibited.

exterior environments visible through wi.rule: Exterior environments visible through windows must use realistic, high-fidelity assets; low-poly or placeholder trees and ground planes are prohibited in final renders.

entrance halls must be furnished with ap.rule: Entrance halls must be furnished with appropriate items (shoe cabinet, console, lighting) to avoid looking like bare shells; the furniture agent must verify that all halls have a minimum set of decorative and functional pieces.

staircases and railings must be selected.rule: Staircases and railings must be selected from a catalogue of styled models that match the project's design language; generic or default placeholder models are prohibited.

interior cameras must be positioned to s.rule: Interior cameras must be positioned to show the room's layout and key furniture, avoiding close-up corner shots that cut off main pieces.

all doors must be modeled with frames an.rule: All doors must be modeled with frames and hardware (handles, hinges) to appear finished; flat slab doors without details are prohibited.

furniture within a room must be stylisti.rule: Furniture within a room must be stylistically coherent; the furniture agent must ensure that major pieces (sofa, bench, etc.) share a common style or material palette.

lighting fixtures must match the room's.rule: Lighting fixtures must match the room's style; the furniture agent must select lamps that are stylistically consistent with the other furniture in the room.

interior cameras must be positioned to s.rule: Interior cameras must be positioned to show key architectural features like windows and daylight sources.

main entrance doors must be modeled with.rule: Main entrance doors must be modeled with full detail (handles, texture, frame) and must match the house's exterior style; generic flat slabs are prohibited.

window and door frames must be colored t.rule: Window and door frames must be colored to match or complement the facade; generic flat grey frames are prohibited if they clash with the building's color scheme.

ground surfaces must have texture and de.rule: Ground surfaces must have texture and detail to avoid a 'video game' aesthetic; flat untextured planes are prohibited in final renders.

an interior camera must be placed inside.rule: An interior camera must be placed inside its room, at eye height 1.2-1.6 m, at least 0.6 m from any door, and aimed at the room's main furniture group, not a blank wall.

kitchen counters and wall cabinets must.rule: Kitchen counters and wall cabinets must be built with textured, styled models that include integrated appliances (cooktop, sink) and finishes matching the project's style, not flat untextured white placeholders.

furniture in a living room must be selec.rule: Furniture in a living room must be selected from a cohesive set or style family; if a piece clashes with the main sofa and other seating, it must be swapped for a model that matches the room's established style.

furniture in a bedroom or living space m.rule: Furniture in a bedroom or living space must be selected from a cohesive set or style family; if a piece clashes with the room's color palette and style, it must be swapped for a model that matches.

furniture models must be high-quality, f.rule: Furniture models must be high-quality, finished assets; low-poly placeholder boxes with grid textures are not acceptable for client presentation.

kitchen counters must be connected to wa.rule: Kitchen counters must be connected to walls or islands to form a coherent set; isolated bare slabs are not acceptable.

exterior renders must use high-quality l.rule: Exterior renders must use high-quality landscaping models (trees, ground) and accurate architectural details; crude 'lollipop' trees and flat untextured ground are not acceptable for client presentation.

exterior views from interior windows mus.rule: Exterior views from interior windows must show a high-quality landscape, not crude low-poly 'lollipop' trees.

a kitchen render must show its anchor ap.rule: A kitchen render must show its anchor appliances (cooktop, fridge, wall cabinets) and the exterior visible through its windows must use the project's site model, not a placeholder landscape.

an interior camera must be placed inside.rule: An interior camera must be placed inside its room, aimed at the room's main furniture group, with a lens that frames the whole group, not a blank wall.

a living room (salon) must contain its m.rule: A living room (salon) must contain its main seating group (sofa, coffee table, armchairs) and a dining set; the exterior visible through its windows must use the project's site model.

a bathroom render must show its fixtures.rule: A bathroom render must show its fixtures and accessories, and the exterior visible through its windows must use the project's site model, not a placeholder landscape.

furniture in a room must be from a coher.rule: Furniture in a room must be from a coherent collection (matching style and scale); the exterior visible through its windows must use the project's site model.

a hall/entrance must contain its functio.rule: A hall/entrance must contain its functional pieces (shoe cabinet, etc.) and decor; the exterior visible through its windows must use the project's site model.

every interior camera must be placed ins.rule: Every interior camera must be placed inside its room's clear volume (at least 0.5 m from any wall or piece) and aimed at the room's centre, so the render shows the room's function, not a wall or a door face.

a decor item that penetrates its host by.rule: A decor item that penetrates its host by more than 0.03 m must be re-seated (or removed) in the next furniture round rather than left unbuilt.

a sideboard or console must be centred o.rule: A sideboard or console must be centred on its wall span (or paired with a companion piece) so the composition is balanced, not pushed into a corner with a bare wall beside it.

a single armchair must be placed as part.rule: A single armchair must be placed as part of a seating group (facing the coffee table or sofa), not flat against a wall under a window.

a washbasin must be anchored to a counte.rule: A washbasin must be anchored to a counter or wall (its base resting on a surface), never floating; if the model reads as a floating slab, re-seat it in the next round.

the exterior ground must carry a real gr.rule: The exterior ground must carry a real ground material (grass, soil, paving) rather than a flat untextured plane.

the dwg reader must read attdef (attribu.rule: The DWG reader must read ATTDEF (attribute definition) entities and map them to the block/label they define, so attribute text is not silently dropped from the ledger.

site decor read on an upper level must b.rule: Site decor read on an upper level must be placed on that level's site (or explicitly suppressed with a reason), not silently dropped because the site is modelled at the ground floor.

when a room outline holds two labels, th.rule: When a room outline holds two labels, the reading must split it into two rooms at the label boundary rather than keeping one label as a second name of the other room.

every printed area label in the document.rule: Every printed area label in the documents must be matched to its room and used in the area check, so a printed area is never silently lost.

when walls are drawn as face lines, the.rule: When walls are drawn as face lines, the reader must also consider wall primitives on runner-up layers (e.g. DUVAR) and off-layer primitives, not only the chosen layer, so no wall segment is left out.

a drawn object in a room that the plan s.rule: A drawn object in a room that the plan shows must be typed and built; if it cannot be typed, it must be recorded with evidence rather than silently dropped.

the reading stage must assign a type to.rule: The reading stage must assign a type to every drawn piece in a furnished room before the build stage; a piece that cannot be typed from its crop is flagged for review and never silently dropped as 'unknown'.

the reading stage must type all drawn pi.rule: The reading stage must type all drawn pieces before the build stage; the build must never skip a piece on the grounds that it is untyped, but instead route it to a review queue so the loss is visible.

a piece whose type is not allowed in its.rule: A piece whose type is not allowed in its room must be re-typed by the reading stage to a type the room allows (or removed if it is not furniture) before the build; it must never be kept unverified.

when one room outline holds the labels o.rule: When one room outline holds the labels of two rooms, the reading stage must split the outline at the missing wall so each room gets its own outline and label.

a small drawn piece that sits around a l.rule: A small drawn piece that sits around a level-mark text (e.g. '+0,50') is a level-mark symbol, not furniture: the reading must mark it as a symbol so the fit stage never places it.

a drawn piece that ends up standing in a.rule: A drawn piece that ends up standing in a doorway (outside the room outline) must be moved to the nearest free place in its room, clear of the door swing, rather than left overlapping a neighbour.

a furniture piece that covers a window o.rule: A furniture piece that covers a window opening (door ray hits the furniture) must be moved to the nearest free place in its room, clear of the window.

elevation-to-plan opening checks require.rule: Elevation-to-plan opening checks require a north arrow (view bearing) on the elevation sheet; when the drawing has none, the check must be skipped with a recorded reason rather than left as an open failure.

a drawn section whose ends do not run on.rule: A drawn section whose ends do not run one-to-one with the plan (offset > 0.30 m) cannot be checked point-by-point against the roof; the check must be skipped with a recorded reason instead of forcing a mismatch.
a drawn section whose ends do not run on.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

an elevation that has neither a view bea.rule: An elevation that has neither a view bearing nor a side label cannot be compared with the model; the render check must skip it with a recorded reason rather than report it as a failure.

when a nightstand's drawn position is 0..rule: When a nightstand's drawn position is 0.06 m off the wall and no free wall span exists within 1.2 m of the drawn place (blocked by doors/windows), the fit stage must accept the drawn position as-is rather than loop on refused moves.

the agent must only propose facade mater.rule: The agent must only propose facade material look-ids that exist in the project's material vocabulary; before calling set_material it must query the available looks and pick one from that list.

when the fitting stage falls back to a p.rule: When the fitting stage falls back to a parametric mesh for a kitchen fitting because no library model matches, the run must record a library_gap warning so the library can be extended, rather than silently building a below-library-level mesh.

When the fitting stage falls back to a parametric mesh for a wall cabinet because no library model matches, the run must record a library_gap warning so the library can be extended, rather than silently building a below-library-level mesh.

bathroom fixtures (tiles, basins, etc.).rule: Bathroom fixtures (tiles, basins, etc.) must use library models with appropriate textures and finishes for client-ready renders; when only plain parametric meshes are available, the run must flag a library_gap rather than ship an institutional-looking fixture.

bed models in the library must include a.rule: Bed models in the library must include a substantial headboard or frame for client-ready renders; a basic low-profile platform without styling is below the quality bar and should be flagged as a library_gap.

nightstand models in the library must ha.rule: Nightstand models in the library must have a cohesive, high-end design that matches the room's furniture set; a plain boxy design that looks identical to a basic first nightstand is below the quality bar and should be flagged as a library_gap.

door models in the library must include.rule: Door models in the library must include styled handles and finishes appropriate for a stylish project; a plain flat slab with a basic handle is below the quality bar for client-ready renders and should be flagged as a library_gap.

exterior plinths and facade wall surface.rule: Exterior plinths and facade wall surfaces must carry a material look (stone, render, brick) matching the project style; bare untextured surfaces are not acceptable for a client presentation.

site paving and paths must use a texture.rule: Site paving and paths must use a textured material model, not a rough untextured mesh, to avoid a placeholder look in renders.

untyped drawn pieces must be marked as n.rule: Untyped drawn pieces must be marked as not furniture with evidence, not left unhandled.

labelled site areas (veranda, balcony) w.rule: Labelled site areas (veranda, balcony) with drawn outlines must be built as site elements, not left as records only.

when a furniture label in the documents.rule: When a furniture label in the documents names a piece type that is not in the room's program and no drawn piece of that type exists within 1 m of the label, the label is treated as an annotation and not enforced as a missing piece.

a labelled outdoor area (veranda, terrac.rule: A labelled outdoor area (veranda, terrace, balcony) in the documents must be built as a site platform with its own outline, floor and railings, and must be listed in the site areas of the level it belongs to.

a room typed 'living' must contain a sof.rule: A room typed 'living' must contain a sofa (or equivalent primary seating) in addition to any dining set; a living room with only armchairs is incomplete.

a kitchen must have a continuous worktop.rule: A kitchen must have a continuous worktop with visible handles and material variation; a row of identical blank boxes is not an acceptable kitchen counter.

a dressing room must have adequate light.rule: A dressing room must have adequate lighting and at least two pieces of furniture (e.g., wardrobe + bench or mirror) to be functional.

a door on an upper level must be reachab.rule: A door on an upper level must be reachable by a stair, lift, or walkway; a door floating above the ground with no access is a critical error.

a staircase must have handrails or balus.rule: A staircase must have handrails or balustrades on at least one side; an open staircase with no railings is a safety hazard.

outdoor vegetation visible through windo.rule: Outdoor vegetation visible through windows must use high-quality models, not low-poly wireframe placeholders.

furniture wood tones must be consistent.rule: Furniture wood tones must be consistent within a room; a third clashing wood tone is a design error.

a salon should have varied seating (sofa.rule: A salon should have varied seating (sofa + armchairs), not four identical chairs; and all seating must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door.

all seating must be reachable by a 0.60.rule: All seating must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door.

all kitchen work surfaces must be reacha.rule: All kitchen work surfaces must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door.

a main entrance door must have visible h.rule: A main entrance door must have visible hardware (handle, frame, leaf) and be legible in renders; a flat white slab is not an acceptable entrance.

all doors must be connected by a 0.60 m.rule: All doors must be connected by a 0.60 m walkway; a door that is not reachable by a walkway is a circulation error.

a labelled outdoor area (veranda, balcon.rule: A labelled outdoor area (veranda, balcony, terrace) in the documents must be built as a platform with a floor and a railing, even when the plan outline is faint; a 'no outline' reason is not a valid excuse to drop a labelled site area.

a room typed as a dressing room or stora.rule: A room typed as a dressing room or storage must be furnished with at least a mirror, a bench and a light source, and its render exposure must be within the cap; a single wardrobe in a dark box is not an acceptable dressing room.

a room typed as living must be furnished.rule: A room typed as living must be furnished with at least a sofa, a coffee table and a TV or media unit; a single sofa and lamp is not an acceptable living room.

a hall or entrance room larger than 8 m2.rule: A hall or entrance room larger than 8 m2 must be furnished with at least a console, a mirror or a light fixture; a bare corridor with only a shoe cabinet and a stair is not an acceptable entrance hall.

a bathroom camera must be positioned to.rule: A bathroom camera must be positioned to show all fixtures with clearance; a camera jammed against the basin or toilet is not an acceptable bathroom view.

a washing machine is not a typical bathr.rule: A washing machine is not a typical bathroom fixture; it belongs in a utility or laundry area. A bathroom render must show all fixtures with clearance, not a cluttered corner.

a master bedroom must not be furnished w.rule: A master bedroom must not be furnished with an office set (desk + office chair); those belong in a study or office. A bedroom render must show the bed and the seating with clearance, not a cluttered office corner.

a children's room larger than 15 m2 must.rule: A children's room larger than 15 m2 must be furnished with at least a bed, a desk, a chair and a rug; a single double bed, a dresser and a nightstand is not an acceptable children's room.

a salon or living room larger than 30 m2.rule: A salon or living room larger than 30 m2 must be furnished with at least a sofa, a coffee table and a TV or media unit; a bare dining room with four identical armchairs is not an acceptable salon.

a kitchen counter must have handles and.rule: A kitchen counter must have handles and material variation; a row of identical blank boxes is not an acceptable kitchen counter. A kitchen render must show the counter, the sink, the stove and the dining set with clearance, not a bare, unfinished box.

a bathtub must have a shower head, a fau.rule: A bathtub must have a shower head, a faucet and a bath mat; a bare bathtub is not an acceptable bathroom fixture. A bathroom render must show the bathtub, the toilet and the washbasin with clearance, not a bare, unfinished box.

a door on an upper level must be reachab.rule: A door on an upper level must be reachable by a stair, a ramp or a balcony; a door 3.50 m above the ground with nothing to reach it is a door into the air and must not be built.

a door-to-door circulation path must kee.rule: A door-to-door circulation path must keep a 0.60 m clear walkway; furniture placed in the path is a fit error, not a clearance tolerance.

a bed's headboard must rest on a wall; a.rule: A bed's headboard must rest on a wall; a headboard floating 0.06 m off the wall is a placement error.

furniture must not block a door's swing.rule: Furniture must not block a door's swing or approach; a bed blocking a door is a placement error.

furniture must not block a window's acce.rule: Furniture must not block a window's access or view; a wardrobe blocking a window is a placement error.

a door-to-window circulation path must k.rule: A door-to-window circulation path must keep a 0.60 m clear walkway; furniture placed in the path is a fit error.

a door-to-door circulation path must kee.rule: A door-to-door circulation path must keep a 0.60 m clear walkway; furniture placed in the path is a fit error.

a desk must have visible legs or a suppo.rule: A desk must have visible legs or a support structure; a floating slab is a model error.

a bathroom must have a visible washbasin.rule: A bathroom must have a visible washbasin; a missing sink is a fundamental design error.

a kitchen must have a functional worktop.rule: A kitchen must have a functional worktop with a hob, sink, and upper cabinets; bare base cabinets are incomplete.

a kitchen must have its main functional.rule: A kitchen must have its main functional pieces (stove, fridge, wall cabinets) built and visible.

a 55 m2 living room must have a sofa and.rule: A 55 m2 living room must have a sofa and dining set as anchor pieces; only armchairs and a coffee table are insufficient.

a 55.6 m2 salon must have a sofa and cof.rule: A 55.6 m2 salon must have a sofa and coffee table as anchor pieces; a dining set alone is insufficient.

a bathroom render must show its main fix.rule: A bathroom render must show its main fixtures (washbasin, toilet, bathtub); a camera that misses the washbasin is a framing error.

a kitchen render must show its main func.rule: A kitchen render must show its main functional pieces (stove, fridge, kitchen counter); a camera that misses them is a framing error.

a bathroom render must show its main fix.rule: A bathroom render must show its main fixtures (shower, toilet, washbasin); a camera that misses the shower is a framing error.

a q4 'missing from the render' finding i.rule: A Q4 'missing from the render' finding is a camera problem, not a build problem, when the facts list the piece in the room; fix the camera, do not relayout or retype.

a q4 'absent' finding is a camera proble.rule: A Q4 'absent' finding is a camera problem, not a build problem, when the facts list the piece in the room; fix the camera, do not relayout or retype.

a dressing room (soyunma odası) smaller.rule: A dressing room (soyunma odası) smaller than 6 m2 is a storage room, not a dressing room: type it storage and place a wardrobe, not a dressing group with bench and mirror.

a q4 'no sofa and no dining set' finding.rule: A Q4 'no sofa and no dining set' finding is a camera problem, not a build problem, when the facts list those pieces in the room; fix the camera, do not relayout or retype.

a q4 'no dining table in frame' finding.rule: A Q4 'no dining table in frame' finding is a camera problem, not a build problem, when the facts list the table in the room; fix the camera, do not retype or swap the model.

a q4 'sink and counter not visible' find.rule: A Q4 'sink and counter not visible' finding is a camera problem, not a build problem, when the facts list those pieces in the room; fix the camera, do not retype or swap the model.

a bedroom smaller than 12 m2 with a slop.rule: A bedroom smaller than 12 m2 with a sloped ceiling is a single-bed room or a study, not a double-bed room: type it accordingly and place a single bed or a desk, not a sofa.

a labelled space outside the walls is bu.rule: A labelled space outside the walls is built as its label says: BALKON is a balcony (open platform off a room), VERANDA is a veranda (covered porch); do not swap the two.

a door on an upper floor (l1 or higher).rule: A door on an upper floor (L1 or higher) must have a way to reach it: a balcony, terrace, external stair or ramp; a door 3.50 m above the ground with nothing to reach it is a door into the air.

a staircase must have handrails or balus.rule: A staircase must have handrails or balustrades on both open sides; a parametric stair without guards is a fall risk and must be built with them.

a kitchen sink must be built with a basi.rule: A kitchen sink must be built with a basin, a counter and visible plumbing; a parametric model that shows only a tap on a block is not a sink.

a room with no window and no artificial.rule: A room with no window and no artificial light source is too dark for a camera; it needs a window, a light fixture or a higher lighting cap.

rule c1 (clearance) must require a walkw.rule: Rule C1 (clearance) must require a walkway of at least 0.80 m along the main circulation path from the entrance door to the first interior door, and at least 0.60 m between any two doors in the same room; a walkway below these minima is a defect to be fixed by moving the blocking piece, not accepted.

rules f2/f3 (furniture placement) must f.rule: Rules F2/F3 (furniture placement) must forbid any furniture piece from blocking a door's swing or the 0.60 m clear zone in front of a door; a piece that blocks a door is a defect to be moved, not accepted.

rule e1 (doors) must require that every.rule: Rule E1 (doors) must require that every door is reachable: its threshold must be at or below 0.15 m above the floor of the room it opens into, or a stair/ramp must be present; a door more than 0.15 m above the floor with no access is a defect.

an interior camera must be placed at a f.rule: An interior camera must be placed at a free point with headroom that shows the room's main furniture group, not pressed against a wall or cabinet face; the show list must include the room's principal pieces.

An interior camera must be placed at a free point with headroom that shows the room's main furniture group, not positioned so a blank wall fills the frame; the show list must include the room's principal pieces.

a bed model must have a realistic duvet.rule: A bed model must have a realistic duvet and pillow geometry, not a crude melted-looking blob; the model must match the room's style and fit the sloped ceiling.

a bed model must have a realistic mattre.rule: A bed model must have a realistic mattress, duvet, and frame geometry, not a crude low-poly mesh; the model must match the room's style and fit the sloped ceiling.

a bed model must match the room's warm w.rule: A bed model must match the room's warm wood and beige palette, not clash with it; the model must fit the room's style and the sloped ceiling.

a sofa model must have realistic texture.rule: A sofa model must have realistic texture and form, not a crude low-poly white block; the model must match the room's style and fit the sloped ceiling.

an interior camera must be placed at a f.rule: An interior camera must be placed at a free point with headroom that shows the room and its main group, not jammed against a door/wardrobe corner; the show list must include the room's principal pieces.
An interior camera must be placed at a free point with headroom that shows the room's main furniture group, including all principal pieces; the show list must include the room's principal pieces.

exterior trees must use realistic, high-.rule: Exterior trees must use realistic, high-poly models with natural foliage, not low-poly 'lollipop' placeholders; the site stage must select models that match the photoreal render quality.

scene check s2 must pass for all element.rule: Scene check S2 must pass for all elements on a level; a failure indicates a geometry error in the build that must be corrected before the render.

scene check s3 must pass for all element.rule: Scene check S3 must pass for all elements on a level; a failure indicates a geometry error in the build that must be corrected before the render.

the main walkway from the entrance door.rule: The main walkway from the entrance door must be at least 0.80 m wide; a piece that blocks the walkway must be moved to a free place in its room, clear of the doorway.

a seating piece whose front use zone is.rule: A seating piece whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door must be re-placed by the room solver, not nudged by hand.

a drawn sanitary or kitchen fixture whos.rule: A drawn sanitary or kitchen fixture whose back is off its wall by more than tolerance must be re-solved with its kitchen run, not swapped for a model that hides the gap.

two kitchen counters that overlap are a.rule: Two kitchen counters that overlap are a mis-solved kitchen run; the run must be re-solved as one unit, not patched piece by piece.

a kitchen counter that reaches through t.rule: A kitchen counter that reaches through the room outline into a door opening is a mis-solved run; the run must be re-solved clear of the door.

a kitchen counter whose front use zone i.rule: A kitchen counter whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door must be re-solved with its run, not moved alone.

a drawn bathtub whose back is off its wa.rule: A drawn bathtub whose back is off its wall by more than tolerance must be re-solved with its bathroom set, not swapped for a model that hides the gap.

a drawn washbasin whose back is off its.rule: A drawn washbasin whose back is off its wall by more than tolerance must be re-solved with its bathroom set, not swapped for a model that hides the gap.

a seating piece whose front use zone is.rule: A seating piece whose front use zone is blocked by another piece must be re-placed by the room solver, not nudged by hand.

a main walkway below 0.80 m between two.rule: A main walkway below 0.80 m between two doors is a clearance failure of the room's layout; the room must be re-solved to open the walkway.

a main walkway below 0.80 m between a do.rule: A main walkway below 0.80 m between a door and a window is a clearance failure of the room's layout; the room must be re-solved to open the walkway.

a drawn dresser whose back is off its wa.rule: A drawn dresser whose back is off its wall by more than tolerance must be re-placed by the room solver, not fixed as a fixture.

a nightstand that overlaps its bed by mo.rule: A nightstand that overlaps its bed by more than tolerance must be re-placed by the room solver, not moved by hand beyond the drawn lock.

a bed with less than 0.60 m free along i.rule: A bed with less than 0.60 m free along its side must be re-placed by the room solver, not swapped for a model that hides the clearance.

a wardrobe whose front use zone is not r.rule: A wardrobe whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door must be re-placed by the room solver, not nudged by hand.

a shower that stands in front of a windo.rule: A shower that stands in front of a window (blocking its light) must be re-placed by the room solver, not swapped for a model that hides the blockage.

a room's furniture layout must leave the.rule: A room's furniture layout must leave the full free zone in front of each seating piece clear of other pieces; a floor lamp or side table may not stand in the sofa's front clearance.

a floor lamp must not stand in front of.rule: A floor lamp must not stand in front of a window sill; it is placed beside the seating, not between the window and the room.

a fixture back within 0.05 m of a wall i.rule: A fixture back within 0.05 m of a wall is on the wall; the off-wall check tolerance is 5 cm.

a washbasin's back must rest on a wall;.rule: A washbasin's back must rest on a wall; a 0.07 m gap is a placement error, not a tolerance.

a washing machine's front use zone must.rule: A washing machine's front use zone must be reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the room door; it is not placed in a corner that blocks the aisle.

the exterior environment must be a belie.rule: The exterior environment must be a believable, textured setting (ground, trees, path) for a client presentation, not a flat placeholder plane with low-poly trees.

a large opening in a wall must be built.rule: A large opening in a wall must be built with a frame and a proper head/sill (or a designed lintel), never as a raw unframed hole with a floating bar; the build stage must add the frame geometry for every opening.

an armchair is part of a seating arrange.rule: An armchair is part of a seating arrangement facing the coffee table, not pushed flat against a wall under a window.

the view outside a window must show a be.rule: The view outside a window must show a believable, textured site, not a flat placeholder plane with low-poly trees.

a piece placed by the decor stage must s.rule: A piece placed by the decor stage must survive the agent stage; the agent must not drop a placed shoe_cabinet without naming it.
A piece placed by the decor stage must survive the agent stage; the agent must not drop a placed desk without naming it.
A piece placed by the decor stage must survive the agent stage; the agent must not drop a placed office_chair without naming it.

a stove is a standalone appliance with i.rule: A stove is a standalone appliance with its own model, not a module of the kitchen_counter run; the build stage must give it a real stove model.

a fridge is a standalone appliance with.rule: A fridge is a standalone appliance with its own model, not a module of the kitchen_counter run; the build stage must give it a real fridge model.

a drawn piece whose label names a type (.rule: A drawn piece whose label names a type (e.g. SIFONIYER) must be typed from that label, not left untyped for review; and a piece that reaches through its room outline is a misread wall, so the room outline is corrected before the piece is placed.

a label that names a furniture type in a.rule: A label that names a furniture type in a room with no piece at its anchor is a missing piece and must be added, not dropped as an exterior camera.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces, not a single untyped piece; it must be split into its member pieces and typed, not marked not-furniture.

a room outline that holds two labels (e..rule: A room outline that holds two labels (e.g. SALON and YEMEK BÖLÜMÜ) is a wall the reading missed; the room must be split so each label is its own room.

the upper landing of a stair that arrive.rule: The upper landing of a stair that arrives at a level must be built as a fixture at that level's landing, not dropped as 'no level above'; a stair's top end is part of the stair, not a separate piece to be re-placed.

strokes on the furniture layer that form.rule: Strokes on the furniture layer that form a recognisable group (a sofa, chairs around a table) must be read as pieces, not left as unused strokes; the reading must group strokes into pieces before the build.

a room outline that holds two labels (e..rule: A room outline that holds two labels (e.g. MUTFAK and ANTRE) is a wall the reading missed; the room must be split so each label is its own room.

a door drawn on an elevation must be mat.rule: A door drawn on an elevation must be matched to a door in the plan and built; an elevation door with no plan counterpart is a reading loss and must be added to the plan and built.

a nightstand that is a necessary piece o.rule: A nightstand that is a necessary piece of a bedroom must be built; when it conflicts with the bed, the bed or the nightstand is re-placed (the bed is the larger, movable piece) so the nightstand fits, not dropped.

a labelled site area (veranda, balkon) o.rule: A labelled site area (VERANDA, BALKON) outside the outer walls must be built as a site area with its outline, even when no walls are drawn around it; the label alone is enough to build the outline.

a kitchen's dining table is redundant wh.rule: A kitchen's dining table is redundant when the salon already has one; the kitchen must be furnished as a kitchen (worktop, hob, fridge, sink) and the redundant dining table removed.

a dressing room must be furnished as a d.rule: A dressing room must be furnished as a dressing room (wardrobe, mirror, bench, lighting), not left with a single wardrobe; the room's program must be completed.

a door on an upper level must be connect.rule: A door on an upper level must be connected to a stair or walkway; a door with nothing to reach it (a door into the air) is a reading error and must be corrected (the door is at the wrong level, or the stair/walkway is missing).

a built stair must include handrails or.rule: A built stair must include handrails or balustrades on both sides; a parametric stair without rails is incomplete and must be built with its rails.

a room typed as a bedroom must contain a.rule: A room typed as a bedroom must contain a bed; if the reading found no bed, the room type is wrong or the bed was lost, and the room must be re-typed or the bed added.

a bathroom whose usable floor is under 7.rule: A bathroom whose usable floor is under 7.5 m2 cannot host a 1.80 m bathtub with the required 0.53 m front clearance; the fixture stage must place a shower or a compact tub instead of a full-size tub in such a room.

the elevation check must compare the num.rule: The elevation check must compare the number of openings on each facade side against the drawn elevation, and flag a mismatch when the model has more openings than the drawing shows.

a bathroom set (bathtub, washbasin, toil.rule: A bathroom set (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) must be solved as one unit so the members do not overlap; when the solver reports no free place within the move limits, the whole set is re-solved, not the single piece.

a piece must not stand in the clear zone.rule: A piece must not stand in the clear zone of a window; when a window ray hits furniture, the blocking piece is moved out of the window's clear zone (the seating group is re-solved away from the window).

a kitchen counter must sit at its workin.rule: A kitchen counter must sit at its working height (about 0.90 m) on the floor; when it is built at the wrong height or partly outside the room, the kitchen run is re-solved so the counter rests on the floor inside the room.

a balcony or veranda labelled in the doc.rule: A balcony or veranda labelled in the documents must be built as a supported slab (with its supports and a door from the room it serves); a floating slab with a railing but no support and no access door is a build error, not a site record.

a downpipe must be modelled with a prope.rule: A downpipe must be modelled with a proper gutter connection at the top and a splash block at the bottom; a bare cylinder is a placeholder and is not an acceptable rain-water detail.

the main entrance must be legible: a cle.rule: The main entrance must be legible: a clear door leaf, handle, canopy or step detail, and an unambiguous porch/landing; when the landing is ambiguous, the entrance solution (steps, ramp, or both) is set explicitly.

every window and door of a room must be.rule: Every window and door of a room must be visible in at least one of the room's camera views; when a view cannot show the required pieces, the room is re-laid out so the pieces are in a place a camera can show, and the camera is then set to show them.

a washbasin must be at a usable working.rule: A washbasin must be at a usable working height (rim about 0.85 m) and reachable; when the current model is too low or wedged, it is swapped for a model of the correct height that fits the room.

a bathroom door must not open directly i.rule: A bathroom door must not open directly into the basin/toilet cluster; the bathroom set is solved so the door swing and the approach to the fixtures are clear.

a stair opening and landing edge must ha.rule: A stair opening and landing edge must have a proper guard (balustrade or glass panel with a handrail and no open gap below); a thin placeholder glass panel with a large open gap is a fall risk and is not an acceptable guard.

a labelled outdoor approach (veranda/ter.rule: A labelled outdoor approach (veranda/terrace) read from the plan must be built as a finished site slab with a material look and, where the level differs from the ground, a set of steps or a ramp; raw untextured geometry is not an acceptable build state for a client-visible outdoor space.

a labelled outdoor space (veranda, balco.rule: A labelled outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) in the documents must be built as a site area with an outline, a floor material, and, where it is open, a railing or guard; it must not be left as a site record only.

a room labelled as a dressing room (soyu.rule: A room labelled as a dressing room (soyunma odası) that is adjacent to a bedroom and holds a wardrobe is typed as a bedroom so its dressing set (wardrobe, mirror, seating) is allowed and completed, not left as a bare 'other' room.

when the section prints the ground floor.rule: When the section prints the ground floor at a non-zero mark (e.g. +0.50), the reading must anchor the building's ground floor to 0.00 m and shift every relative level mark by that offset, so all element heights are read from the correct datum.

the big loop must run at least one fix c.rule: The big loop must run at least one fix cycle when the house score is below target, instead of stopping with zero cycles.

a drawn piece whose size and room do not.rule: A drawn piece whose size and room do not allow its read type (a sofa in a bedroom) is retyped to the type its size and room allow, not kept unverified.

when a room's dressing group has no plac.rule: When a room's dressing group has no place that passes the checks, the solver must relax the dressing group's clearance/footprint constraints for small dressing rooms (or place the mirror and seating against the free wall) rather than leaving the room with only a wardrobe.

a small drawn piece that sits around a l.rule: A small drawn piece that sits around a level-mark text (e.g. '+0,50') is a level-mark symbol, not furniture, and is recorded as such.

views marked for review must be re-check.rule: Views marked for review must be re-checked and corrected (camera pose or content) in a subsequent agent round before the run is accepted.

when a tall wardrobe drawn against a wal.rule: When a tall wardrobe drawn against a wall blocks a door or window and cannot be moved (drawn lock, no free wall span), the solver must either shorten the wardrobe to a model that clears the opening or shift the opening, rather than leaving the blockage.

a kitchen must always contain a hob/stov.rule: A kitchen must always contain a hob/stove and a fridge as part of its kitchen run; if the reading placed them but the group check reports them missing, the solver must re-anchor the kitchen run so the stove and fridge are present and counted, not drop them.

a floor lamp whose model has an oversize.rule: A floor lamp whose model has an oversized shade at head height is swapped for a library model of the same footprint with a correct proportion, not a generated model.

when a washbasin in a small bathroom blo.rule: When a washbasin in a small bathroom blocks a door or window and cannot be moved (fixture move limit, clearance), the solver must reposition the door/window or choose a smaller basin that clears the opening, rather than leaving the blockage.

a large living room (salon) must always.rule: A large living room (salon) must always show its sofa and dining set in at least one interior view; if the camera cannot show them because of walkway constraints, the solver must adjust the furniture layout to free a camera point, not leave the room looking empty.

a shoe cabinet under a sloped ceiling mu.rule: A shoe cabinet under a sloped ceiling must use a model whose height fits under the slope (at most the clearance height); if no library model fits, the solver must resize the cabinet or choose a lower model, not leave a crude placeholder.

the architect's rule f5 must explicitly.rule: The architect's rule F5 must explicitly cover overlapping kitchen counters (e.g. a counter that wraps a corner overlapping another counter segment) so the critic does not flag them as F9.

the architect's rule s4 must specify the.rule: The architect's rule S4 must specify the minimum clear space in front of bathtubs and other wet-room fixtures so the critic's G10 check is aligned with the intended clearance.

the architect's rule f4 must specify tha.rule: The architect's rule F4 must specify that the free zone in front of an armchair may be partially occupied by a floor lamp or small side piece, so the critic does not flag it as blocked.

a tall storage piece (wardrobe, tall_cab.rule: A tall storage piece (wardrobe, tall_cabinet, bookshelf) must not stand in front of a window whose sill is lower than the piece's top; the piece must be moved off the window or the window raised.

a sofa's free zone in front (the viewing.rule: A sofa's free zone in front (the viewing/circulation side) must be clear of other pieces; if a piece blocks it, the sofa or the blocking piece must be moved so the zone is free.

an interior camera must be posed to show.rule: An interior camera must be posed to show the room's main pieces, not a bare corner; if the room is small, the camera shows the furniture that defines it.

the exterior site must not use low-poly.rule: The exterior site must not use low-poly placeholder trees that break the render's realism; if no good tree model is available, the site should have no trees rather than crude ones.

a kitchen counter must not cut a wall by.rule: A kitchen counter must not cut a wall by more than 0.030 m; if it does, it must be moved to a valid spot within the room.

a washbasin model must include its fauce.rule: A washbasin model must include its faucet and be styled to match the room; a bare basin without a faucet looks unfinished.

a bathtub model must include its faucet.rule: A bathtub model must include its faucet and fittings; a bare tub looks like an empty box.

a toilet model must match the room's aes.rule: A toilet model must match the room's aesthetic; a bulky dated two-piece model clashes with a modern bathroom.

a kitchen counter run must not be built.rule: A kitchen counter run must not be built as a row of identical blank boxes; it must have handles, material variation, and appliance integration to read as a designed kitchen, not a parametric placeholder.

a seating group must not be four identic.rule: A seating group must not be four identical chairs; the chairs should vary in model to read as a designed living room, not a showroom display.

a small untyped drawn piece (0.21 x 0.20.rule: A small untyped drawn piece (0.21 x 0.20 m) that is not built and is not furniture should be marked as a non-furniture symbol, not left as an unknown piece.

a dining table model must match the room.rule: A dining table model must match the room's aesthetic and the other furniture; a plain boxy slab clashes with sculptural chairs and warm wood floors.

a coffee table model must match the room.rule: A coffee table model must match the room's palette; a bright honey-oak table clashes with a pale floor and muted upholstery.

a floor lamp model whose shade top sits.rule: A floor lamp model whose shade top sits at or above 1.40 m (head height) and whose shade diameter exceeds 0.45 m is rejected for interior rooms; the fit must pick a model with a shade top between 1.50 and 1.80 m and a shade that does not block the nearest window.

interior views looking out through windo.rule: Interior views looking out through windows must have a site context with at least 4 trees and a textured ground (grass or paving) to avoid the 'lollipop tree and flat green plane' placeholder look.

a hall or entrance room must have an ent.rule: A hall or entrance room must have an entrance group (shoe cabinet, console, or lighting) placed; if the solver cannot place it due to walkway constraints, the room layout must be adjusted to free up space for the entrance group.

a stair model must match the project's s.rule: A stair model must match the project's style; if the current model is a generic placeholder, it should be swapped for a model that expresses the project's design language.

interior camera views must be framed to.rule: Interior camera views must be framed to show the main pieces of furniture in the room; if the camera is too close to a corner or tilted, it should be adjusted to show the room's layout and scale.

doors must have a frame and hardware det.rule: Doors must have a frame and hardware detail; if the current model is a flat slab, it should be swapped for a model with a frame and hardware, or the material should be set to a wood look to add detail.

a wardrobe model must match the project'.rule: A wardrobe model must match the project's style; if the current model is a different style or wood tone, it should be swapped for a model that matches the project's design language.

a floor lamp model must match the projec.rule: A floor lamp model must match the project's style; if the current model is an ornate, turned-wood classic style, it should be swapped for a model that matches the project's neutral and modern feel.

interior camera views must show the wind.rule: Interior camera views must show the windows in the room to provide daylight and context; if the window is not visible, the camera should be adjusted to show it.

the main entrance door must have a handl.rule: The main entrance door must have a handle, texture, or frame detail; if the current model is a generic, flat white slab, it should be swapped for a model with detail, or the material should be set to a wood look to add detail.

window and door frames must match the pr.rule: Window and door frames must match the project's style; if the current frames are a generic, flat grey, they should be set to a material that matches the project's design language (e.g., aluminium anthracite for a modern look).

the ground must be textured (grass, pavi.rule: The ground must be textured (grass, paving, or gravel) to avoid the 'flat, untextured green plane' placeholder look.

interior camera views must be framed to.rule: Interior camera views must be framed to show the main pieces of furniture in the room; if the camera is pointed at a blank wall, it should be adjusted to show the room's main group.
Interior camera views must be framed to show the main fixtures in the room; if the camera is aimed at a blank wall, it should be adjusted to show the room's main fixtures.

a kitchen set must have appliances, cook.rule: A kitchen set must have appliances, cooktop, and styling; if the current model is a flat, untextured white, it should be swapped for a model with detail and texture.

when a seating set in one room mixes sty.rule: When a seating set in one room mixes styles, swap the outlier to a model from the same style family as the anchor piece (sofa), not a taller or differently-proportioned one that fails the fit caps.

when an armchair clashes with the room's.rule: When an armchair clashes with the room's neutral palette, swap to a model in the same style family (minimal/modern/scandinavian) with a neutral color.

exterior renders must have realistic lan.rule: Exterior renders must have realistic landscaping (trees, hedges, paths) and ground cover (grass, paving) to avoid a 'video game' look.

when a fridge model is a flat slab with.rule: When a fridge model is a flat slab with no detail, swap to a model with door splits, handles, and brand detail.

an interior camera of a kitchen must fra.rule: An interior camera of a kitchen must frame the kitchen run, sink and stove, not the adjacent dining/hall side of the room.

a dining table model must match the room.rule: A dining table model must match the room's minimal/modern style and not read as a crude low-poly placeholder.

a dining chair must match the light, min.rule: A dining chair must match the light, minimalist palette of the room, not a dark heavy traditional wood.

a salon's seating group must share one c.rule: A salon's seating group must share one coherent palette and be anchored by a coffee table and rug, not a chaotic mix of clashing mid-century pieces.

sofas in one seating group must share a.rule: Sofas in one seating group must share a coherent colour temperature and style, not a clashing orange against white.

opposite sofas in a seating group must r.rule: Opposite sofas in a seating group must read as a coherent set, not two unrelated styles and colours.

a 55 m2 salon's seating group must be an.rule: A 55 m2 salon's seating group must be anchored by a coffee table and rug so it reads as a designed room, not a half-finished showroom.

a salon must present a unified palette a.rule: A salon must present a unified palette and use its floor area, not a showroom of clashing mid-century pieces over mostly empty floor.

the exterior seen through windows must b.rule: The exterior seen through windows must be a realistic landscape, not a crude low-poly cartoon of lollipop trees on flat ground.

a bathroom must show its washbasin and k.rule: A bathroom must show its washbasin and keep the washing machine clear of the corner, not crammed in.

a toilet must match the clean modern lin.rule: A toilet must match the clean modern lines of the bathroom, not a dated standard model.

the exterior seen through windows and ba.rule: The exterior seen through windows and balcony doors must be a realistic landscape, not a cartoon of flat lollipop trees on flat ground.

an office chair must match the calm ligh.rule: An office chair must match the calm light palette of the bedroom, not a dark bulky model.

a children's room must present a designe.rule: A children's room must present a designed palette and keep storage from dominating the frame or blocking the window.

a bedroom's furniture set must use a sin.rule: A bedroom's furniture set must use a single coherent style family; when two beds are present they must be the same model or a matched pair, and any study furniture must match the room's age-appropriate program.

interior bathroom cameras must be positi.rule: Interior bathroom cameras must be positioned to show the full wet-room set (shower/bathtub, washbasin, toilet) from a free point with headroom, not pressed against a fixture or wall.

bed models must be verified for geometri.rule: Bed models must be verified for geometric integrity (no voids, correct mattress/headboard) before rendering; a broken mesh is a critical defect that must be swapped.

a bedroom's furniture set must be stylis.rule: A bedroom's furniture set must be stylistically coherent; the bed, nightstands, and any desk/chair should share a common design language.

seating in a room must be stylistically.rule: Seating in a room must be stylistically coherent; an office chair should match the style of the other seating (armchairs) in the same room.

all scheduled furniture pieces in a room.rule: All scheduled furniture pieces in a room must be built and visible; a broken bed model must be swapped, and missing pieces must be placed.

doors must have a realistic material and.rule: Doors must have a realistic material and frame details; a plain untextured slab is not acceptable for a client-ready render.

hallway cameras must show the key elemen.rule: Hallway cameras must show the key elements (stair, storage) from a free point that does not emphasize safety hazards like unguarded stair edges.

hallway cameras should be positioned to.rule: Hallway cameras should be positioned to show the corridor's length and key doors, not a corner and a single door leaf.

a bedroom must have a bed; if the room i.rule: A bedroom must have a bed; if the room is furnished as a lounge, it should be retyped or a bed should be added.
